details:
**1MDB scandal**
1Malaysia Development Berhad was a state investment fund set up in 2009 under Prime Minister Najib Razak. Billions of dollars were stolen from it and spent on luxury real estate, art, a yacht, and Hollywood films, making it one of the largest financial scandals in history.

**Jho Low**
The Malaysian financier accused of masterminding the 1MDB theft, including moving money without approval from Malaysia's central bank, Bank Negara. He became known for extravagant parties, including a birthday party where Britney Spears popped out of a cake, and for giving Leonardo DiCaprio a Picasso painting. He remains a fugitive.

**Najib Razak**
Malaysia's prime minister from 2009 to 2018 and leader of the UMNO party. About 700 million dollars from 1MDB-linked sources ended up in his personal accounts. He was arrested in July 2018 after his coalition lost power, and he was later convicted and imprisoned.

**Goldman Sachs**
The investment bank that raised billions in bonds for 1MDB, much of which was stolen. In 2020 Goldman agreed to pay a 2.9 billion dollar penalty to US authorities, and it reached a separate settlement with Malaysia. Its bankers Tim Leissner and Roger Ng faced US charges; Leissner pleaded guilty and Ng was convicted in 2022.

**Malaysia Airlines Flight 370**
A flight from Kuala Lumpur to Beijing that vanished in March 2014 with 239 people aboard. Investigators believe it turned south and crashed in the southern Indian Ocean, but the main wreckage has never been found.

**Malaysia Airlines Flight 17**
A flight from Amsterdam to Kuala Lumpur that was shot down over eastern Ukraine in July 2014, four months after MH370 disappeared, killing all 298 people aboard. An international investigation found it was hit by a Russian Buk missile fired from territory held by Russian-backed separatists.

**Assassination of Kim Jong-nam**
The estranged half-brother of North Korean leader Kim Jong-un was killed with the VX nerve agent at Kuala Lumpur International Airport in February 2017. Two women, Siti Aisyah of Indonesia and Doan Thi Huong of Vietnam, said they believed they were taking part in a TV prank. The murder charge against Siti Aisyah was dropped, and Doan Thi Huong pleaded guilty to a lesser charge.

**Mahathir Mohamad and the 2018 election**
Mahathir, who had already been prime minister from 1981 to 2003, returned at age 92 to lead the opposition Pakatan Harapan coalition to victory in 2018. It was the first time the Barisan Nasional coalition, dominated by UMNO, had lost power since independence.

**Anwar Ibrahim and Reformasi**
Anwar was Mahathir's deputy until he was fired and expelled from UMNO in 1998 and jailed on sodomy and corruption charges widely seen as politically motivated. His supporters launched the Reformasi reform movement. He was pardoned in 2018 and became prime minister in 2022.

**Yang di-Pertuan Agong**
The title of Malaysia's king, who is chosen in rotation from the hereditary rulers of nine Malay states and serves five-year terms. In January 2019, Sultan Muhammad V of Kelantan became the first king to abdicate, after reports that he had married a former Russian beauty queen.

**Petronas Towers**
Twin skyscrapers in Kuala Lumpur that were the tallest buildings in the world from 1998 to 2004. They are named for the state oil company Petronas.

**Bumiputera**
The term, meaning "sons of the soil," for ethnic Malays and other Indigenous peoples of Malaysia. Affirmative action policies favoring Bumiputera over the wealthier ethnic Chinese and Indian minorities are a long-running source of racial tension.

**Fahmi Reza**
A Malaysian graphic artist arrested and convicted for posting a caricature of Najib Razak as a clown in 2016. The image spread widely as a symbol of protest against Najib's government.

**Batu Caves and Kek Lok Si Temple**
The Batu Caves, near Kuala Lumpur, are limestone caves containing a major Hindu temple complex and a giant golden statue of the god Murugan. Kek Lok Si is a large Buddhist temple near George Town on the island of Penang.

**Borneo, Sarawak, and Mount Kinabalu**
Malaysia is split between the Malay Peninsula, east of the Strait of Malacca, and the northern part of the island of Borneo. Its Bornean state of Sarawak borders Brunei and Indonesian Kalimantan, and Mount Kinabalu in the state of Sabah is its highest peak.
